articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers says he's done with Steelers, says Mike McCarthy asleep in meetings
articles.description: Quarterback Aaron Rodgers said Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" that he won't return to the Steelers after his stunning benching and alleges that coach Mike McCarthy has been sleeping in meetings.
articles.body:
Quarterback Aaron Rodgers said Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show" that he won't return to the Pittsburgh Steelers after his stunning benching and alleges that coach Mike McCarthy has been sleeping through team meetings. 

"That ship has sailed," Rodgers said of his time with the Steelers. 

He said he found out from teammate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched and still hasn't heard the news from McCarthy.

Rodgers said Freiermuth told him on a phone call, "I can't believe they're doing this," and Rodgers said he replied "'doing what?'"

Rodgers said his agent has been in contact with Steelers general manager Omar Khan, however. 

The four-time MVP said he had extensive conversations with McCarthy over the past two days, and the word "benching" never came up.

Rodgers then went on to recount his past week with McCarthy and said the coach was "snoring" in team meetings and said this was "not an abnormal week."

"Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened," Rodgers said.

He then went on to describe what happened on Sunday when the Steelers struggled in a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

"... there was some guys early on that didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys that Mike didn't want to get to know the defense. At one point I told him, 'You should really lean into the defensive guys a little bit more and talk to those guys.' And he said, 'Well, I don't think I need to.' And I said, 'Well, I disagree with that.' So, a lot of those guys, he kind of already lost a lot of those guys. And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it, we're kind of on the offense on one side of defense on the other side. And there's some rambling or something and without even a heads up, he says, 'All right, one, two, three Packers.'

"That's what he broke it down on in the locker room."

Rodgers said he and his teammates "looked around going, "What the f---? What is going on? Where's his head at at this point?'"

Rodgers said he and McCarthy talked on Monday, and he said to the coach, "'Hey, this last week, this is not what we talked about. We've had these conversations for months now and it began as a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy. If you're not coming to everything, you should be coming to as a playcaller.'"

articles.headline: Will the Rams be able to slow down the Packers' passing game?
articles.description: Odds, analysis and recommended plays to help you bet the Thanksgiving eve Packers-Rams game.
articles.body:
The NFL's Thanksgiving week starts in L.A. on Wednesday night with the Los Angeles Rams hosting the Green Bay Packers in a critical NFC matchup. Let's take a quick look at both clubs before picking our bets.

The Packers feature the league's most vertical-based passing game, as quarterback Jordan Love has attempted a league-high 63 throws of 20 or more air yards. The test here is that the Rams' defense (and pass rush) allows only 187.7 passing yards per game (third fewest). Can Green Bay create some sense of a rushing element in this one to set up the shot-play throws to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden?

Mike LaFleur's club ranks dead last in the league with only 67 yards rushing per game. For the Rams, this is a transition period on offense, with top receivers Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR. Expect more multiple tight end sets versus Green Bay and a foundational run game approach, as both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum will see volume, which creates play-action and boot opportunities for Matthew Stafford. But keep eyes on a Green Bay defense that has forced 20 turnovers this season (second most). And don't forget, edge rusher Micah Parsons is slated to make his season debut.

Notable player prop odds, best bets

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Packers +2.5 (-104)

I'll take the points with Green Bay. Winning early downs on defense will be key, as the Packers can dial up some pressure in passing situations to dent the pocket versus Stafford. Plus, I expect LaFleur to have answers here to create explosive plays.

Matthew Golden receptions OVER 5.5 receptions (-110)

Golden has six or more receptions in five of his last six games, and he's averaging 10.7 targets per game during that stretch. With the anticipated volume, Golden can be deployed as a target for Love at all three levels of the field versus the Rams.

articles.headline: Commanders and WR Brandon Aiyuk: What to expect, his fit and fantasy impact
articles.description: Our experts answer the biggest questions surrounding Aiyuk agreeing to join the Commanders practice squad.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Brandon Aiyuk advertised his desire to play for Washington quite often this year. He posted pictures of himself in Commanders gear. He said he bought a $10 million house in Loudoun County, Virginia, where Washington trains.

It wasn't exactly a secret.

The only question became whether that desire would be shared by the Commanders -- and, depending on the social media post, it seemed to ebb and flow over the past seven or eight months. They long had their eye on him as someone who could provide more juice to their offense, if he were healthy.

On Wednesday, Aiyuk agreed to a deal to join the Commanders' practice squad. If that leads to Aiyuk playing for Washington, the question becomes: What now? He hasn't played since Oct. 20, 2024, after tearing his ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee. Can he actually return to the NFL without having practiced since that time and contribute? If so, how quickly?

And can he ever again become the player he was in 2023, when he caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns en route to being named second-team All-Pro?

That's what both sides may be about to find out.

Commanders reporter John Keim, 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner, NFL analyst Matt Bowen and Fantasy analyst Mike Florio weigh in on everything you need to know.

Why Aiyuk? And why now?

Because he was available. And if he hits, he can become the No. 1 receiver in 2027 with Terry McLaurin's future in Washington uncertain. McLaurin tore the patellar tendon in his left knee in Week 6 and has a $34 million cap hit next season. Not only is his return date unknown, but so will be his ability to play at a certain level.

That's why they need to explore their options to find someone who can provide some help now but be a top option in 2027 and beyond. One team source said they know how hard it can be to find an elite receiver in free agency so they need to be creative, whether through trades, the draft or a signing like this one.

If they're fortunate, he can contribute down the stretch for a team that became more interesting after a 22-20 win over Cincinnati on Monday night. At 4-5-1 the Commanders can contend for a playoff spot over the final seven games; perhaps he can contribute at some point to help them achieve that goal.

They also have two key people who know him well: quarterback Jayden Daniels and general manager Adam Peters.

Daniels and Aiyuk played together at Arizona State and have remained close, even through a rough patch this summer when Aiyuk put out multiple social media posts directed at Daniels and, in one, his mother.

Peters was an assistant general manager in San Francisco with Aiyuk from 2020 to '23. He would know how Aiyuk gets along in the locker room and would be well-suited to get intel from people with whom he remains close in the organization, including coach Kyle Shanahan.

articles.headline: Ex-Bucks guard Kevin Porter Jr. finalizing 2-year deal to join Magic, agent says
articles.description: Free agent guard Kevin Porter Jr. is finalizing a two-year contract with the Magic, his agent told ESPN.
articles.body:
Free agent guard Kevin Porter Jr. is finalizing a two-year contract with the Orlando Magic, his agent, Sam Permut of Roc Nation, told ESPN.

Porter held meetings with the Denver Nuggets and then the Magic earlier this week. Both teams have been searching for backcourt depth and discussed deals for Porter, who averaged 17.4 points and 7.4 assists per game last season with the Milwaukee Bucks.

Magic officials conducted extensive due diligence as part of the process with 26-year-old Porter, sources told ESPN.

The Nuggets nearly traded for Porter before the regular season started, offering Zeke Nnaji, two second-round draft picks and a second-round pick swap to Milwaukee, according to sources. The Bucks declined Denver's offer due to the additional year on Nnaji's deal for $7.46 million next season.

The deal comes just over a month after the Bucks waived Porter before the start of the regular season. The six-year veteran joins a Magic squad that has lost three of its last four games and lacks backcourt depth behind the starting trio of Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane and Anthony Black.

The Bucks had a surplus of guards at the time, as they were retooling in their first season without two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo. Waiving Porter opened up playing time for younger guards like rookie Brayden Burries and 20-year-old Kasparas Jakučionis, who have helped complement Ryan Rollins and Tyler Herro in Milwaukee's backcourt.

Jakučionis and Herro came to Milwaukee in the Antetokounmpo trade. The Bucks selected Burries out of Arizona with the 10th overall pick in this year's draft.

articles.headline: Brandon Aiyuk joining Commanders, will reunite with college QB Jayden Daniels
articles.description: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Commanders on their practice squad, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders on their practice squad, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Wednesday.

Aiyuk now will once again become teammates with Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, who Aiyuk played with at Arizona State in 2019.

The San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Tuesday, two weeks after the NFL reinstated him. He cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent.

Washington general manager Adam Peters, who was with Aiyuk in San Francisco from 2020 to 2023, praised the receiver during his paid weekly appearance on 106.7 The Fan earlier Wednesday. He called Aiyuk a "smart football player" and said he was one of the "hardest workers on the team" with the 49ers.

"One of the things that I don't think anyone can dispute is his work ethic," Peters said. "That's how he became an All-Pro-type player."

He then discussed Aiyuk's on-field talent, pointing to his final full season of 2023 when he was named second-team All-Pro.

"He was a true No. 1 receiver at the time. He's a guy who's a tough cover, he's great after the catch. There's a lot of great things about him on the field," Peters said. "It wasn't just that he was the most gifted guy; he's self-made too. There's a lot of positives."

Peters said he hasn't talked to Aiyuk in "a couple years."

"I can't speak on all what happened between him and the 49ers," Peters said. "What I do remember is he's a very motivated player."

Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024, and was placed on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list last December. He could not be removed from that list until he reported and passed a physical, which he did Nov. 9.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk told 49ers reporters earlier this month. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100%."

In 2023, his last full season before his injury, Aiyuk was named second-team All-Pro after catching 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

A rift between Aiyuk and Daniels appeared to have developed following a series of social media posts by the receiver. Aiyuk targeted Daniels in several posts and in one referenced Daniels' mother.

However, Daniels and Aiyuk spoke more than a month ago to clear the air, according to multiple sources.

Daniels befriended Aiyuk early in their time together at ASU -- before Daniels had won the starting quarterback job. During workouts, Daniels would throw with Aiyuk, who was going into his senior season and coming off a 33-catch, 474-yard season.

They quickly developed a rapport as Aiyuk ended the season with Associated Press All-America honors after catching 65 passes for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns.

Tonight's games are power-packed for both the Cup and the NBA standings, with five of the nine matchups between two teams that are both .500 or better and competing for league positioning. The first game of the day, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern, features two of the teams that made the biggest moves this offseason in the Miami Heat and the Philadelphia 76ers. The 76ers enter the night as the top seed in the Eastern Conference, but the Heat are the hottest team in the league with seven straight wins and are also in first place in East Group B at 2-0. The 76ers are 1-1, and will need to win to keep pace with the Heat in the Cup standings.

Another major matchup in East Group B reprises the 2026 Eastern Conference Finals, with the Cleveland Cavaliers (2-1 in NBA Cup standings) battling the New York Knicks (0-2). The Knicks started the season slowly but have won five straight to move up in the league standings. But they still have work to do to get back into contention to try to defend their 2025 Emirates NBA Cup championship.

Meanwhile, in West Group B, the 2-0 Minnesota Timberwolves do battle with the 1-1 Oklahoma City Thunder in a matchup of Northwest Division rivals who are both persevering despite major injuries shaking their lineups.

These, and many other storylines will be on display in tonight's action. As always, let's dig deeper into the matchups to identify some potential fantasy streamers and betting angles of interest.

articles.headline: Vinícius Júnior praised by Jude Bellingham: Critics want 'excuse to hammer him'
articles.description: Jude Bellingham backed Vinícius Júnior to silence his critics after the winger shone in Real Madrid's 5-1 Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Jude Bellingham backed Vinícius Júnior to silence his critics after the winger shone in Real Madrid's 5-1 Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.

Brazil international Vinícius has had a tough season -- losing his place in the Madrid team to new signing Yan Diomande and being hit with a four-game ban after being sent off last month -- but impressed after being handed a start against PSV.

Vinícius signed a new long-term deal at the Bernabéu last summer having been linked with a move away, and admitted during the international break that speculation over his future, coupled with the World Cup, had affected his pre-season preparations.

"I thought [Vinícius] had a brilliant game," Bellingham told TNT Sports. "In the first half, everyone was one or two steps off, but in the second half I thought the level of everyone improved massively, and he was fantastic.

"It looked like it was going to be one of those games where he didn't quite get his goal, and I know for him, that kind of stuff will weigh on him at the moment. I think everyone is out to get him a little bit. Everyone wants an excuse to just hammer him.

"I think it was the best moment of the game for us as a club, as a team and for him that he could get that goal, it matched his performance in the second half."

Bernardo Silva on Vinícius Júnior: 'We see him smiling'

Vinícius' 87th-minute strike -- set up by Bellingham -- was his first Champions League goal this season, while he's also only found the net once in LaLiga.

"For the team it's good that he's with a happy face, we see him smiling," midfielder Bernardo Silva told TNT Sports. "He's coming very strong to this part of the season, and we definitely need him. If you want to win big things you have to count on these types of players."

- Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'

- Bellingham credits Mourinho 'full stop' for stellar form after Madrid stunner

- Champions League recap: Arsenal drop points vs. Dortmund, Madrid go top

Bellingham was outstanding against PSV, with coach José Mourinho calling him "the best midfielder in the world."

"[Bellingham] is very special," Silva said. "He's a player who can create something very different at any moment. He was a big part of the way we played in the second half.

"Physically he's very strong, he allows us to get to the second ball and then attack. He's good at everything."

articles.headline: Barcelona to appeal Fermín López's two-match ban - sources
articles.description: Fermín López has been hit with a two-match suspension after getting sent off in Barcelona's comeback win against Villarreal last weekend.
articles.body:
Fermín López has been hit with a two-match suspension after getting sent off in Barcelona's comeback win against Villarreal last weekend.

Fermín, 23, will miss Barça's LaLiga fixtures at Deportivo A Coruña this weekend and the home game against title rivals Atlético Madrid next Wednesday.

Barça plan to appeal the ban, a source told ESPN.

The Spain international was dismissed in the second half of Barça's 3-2 victory at Spotify Camp Nou over Villarreal for protesting a decision after he had been substituted.

Jumping up from the bench, where he was watching the match after coming off, he approached the fourth official to appeal for a penalty after Anthony Gordon went down in the box.

"Are you f------ kidding me?!" he shouted when a spot kick was not awarded.

Fermín then disappeared down the tunnel, preventing referee Alejandro Hernández Hernández from showing him a red card, but the official's post-match report confirmed the midfielder had been sent off.

Speaking ahead of Wednesday's Champions League game against Sabah, Barça coach Hansi Flick joked he may have to re-think where Fermín sits on the bench.

- Jesús Owono: Goalkeeper trains solo amid 12-game ban after Jesús De Miguel death

- Who are Sabah FK, Barcelona's Champions League opponents?

- Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres

"We have two rows, so next time we will have to see where we put the players who are, let's say, very emotional, like Fermín," Flick said.

"We will put them in the last row. I think it's better he has more metres to go! It's not nice that he has the red card because we have a lot of important games coming up."

Fermín started poorly against Villarreal, with his mistake leading to the away team's first goal as they took a shock 2-0 lead inside seven minutes.

However, Barça responded after the break, with Fermín netting the equaliser as the LaLiga leaders came from behind to win 3-2 and make it 12 wins from 13 league games this season.

Fermín has been in fine form across all competitions, scoring nine goals and providing seven assists in 16 appearances.

articles.headline: Newcastle owners not considering full sale, only minority deals - reports
articles.description: Newcastle's Saudi owners are not treating the possibility of selling a minority stake in the club as the first step towards a full sale, the Press Association understands.
articles.body:
Newcastle's Saudi owners are not treating the possibility of selling a minority stake in the club as the first step towards a full sale, sources told Press Association.

The Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), which owns a majority stake in Newcastle, is understood to have enlisted JP Morgan to examine ways to fund the building of a new stadium.

One method to achieve this could be the sale of new shares in the club, with The Athletic reporting that could equate to a new investor holding up to 25% of the club's shares and diluting the PIF's stake.

News of a willingness to consider selling a minority stake may on the surface make fans question the owners' long-term commitment, but sources close to the PIF insist it should not be interpreted that way and that work to finance a new stadium should instead be seen as a signal of the PIF's willingness to remain for the long haul.

- Raheem Sterling avoids jail for dangerous driving

- Transfer rumors, news: Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes eyed by Juventus

- Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Newcastle eye Inter's Pio Esposito

Any serious offer to buy the club would always be considered, sources said, because the PIF is ultimately seeking a financial return as an investment fund. However, that is absolutely not the purpose of the process the PIF is now embarking on with JP Morgan, sources told Press Association.

Earlier this year, the PIF ended its investment in the LIV Golf series, which has since collapsed into bankruptcy.

Newcastle have already announced plans for a new training complex near the city's international airport, but have not yet confirmed whether they will press ahead with building a new stadium.

Newcastle and the PIF have been contacted for comment.
